classification_display.semantics: Native predictive reference compatibility, not accuracy, posterior probability, or FDR. Higher reference values admit more alternatives; source spans are fixed.

comparability.help: Conditional population comparison from native evidence only; no balancing or deletion of calls.
comparability.label: Score CT/GA comparability
comparability.name: enabled

comparability.help: Absolute CT–GA margin for comparability, separate from existence and testability.
comparability.label: Allowed population fraction difference
comparability.name: equivalence_margin

comparability.help: Both conditional fractions must exceed this floor for comparative support.
comparability.label: Population existence floor
comparability.name: existence_floor

compute.help: Start at consolidation: fail on a missing or incompatible native-fit checkpoint instead of fitting again.
compute.label: Require saved native fits
compute.name: require_native_cache

compute.help: CPU reference or opt-in CUDA/MPS interval scoring. Same CPU random draws and probabilities; numerically borderline device results are rechecked on CPU. Unavailable devices fall back explicitly.
compute.label: Predictive scoring backend (vectorized = counter-based generator, declared versioned kernel)
compute.name: predictive_backend

compute.help: Only with predictive_backend=vectorized. 0 = plain Monte Carlo with the counter-based generator; a fraction in (0,1) mixes the generating-projection law with uniform; threshold:M spends draws on projections whose penalty could reach the observed loss within M nats. Unbiased for the same tail in every case; only the variance changes.
compute.label: Vectorized predictive importance tilt
compute.name: predictive_tilt

cr.help: Lattice recaller (the default) finds class geometries by k-means on confident calls and scores every molecule's lattice against them with EM (no Monte Carlo). Staged native families (deprecated) uses lattice-aware Monte Carlo fits and shared-geometry consolidation. Call harmonization is the separate lightweight overlap method. Saved historical engines remain available.
cr.label: Consensus algorithm
cr.name: engine

cr.help: Average-linkage cut on overlap of the shorter footprint. Larger values merge more similar geometries.
cr.label: Native-call clustering distance
cr.name: harmonization_cut

cr.help: Direct non-transitive overlap required to fold a recurrent family into an anchor.
cr.label: Family folding overlap
cr.name: harmonization_fold_overlap

cross.help: All plausible cross-dataset pairs; native nodes and both intervals stay unchanged. At least two datasets required.
cross.label: Build XCR relationship graph
cross.name: enabled

cross.help: Keep fine native classes and additionally report bounded, non-transitive broad-anchor groups. Count each molecule once, even if it carries multiple children. No detection is added.
cross.label: Report coarser ANY-child comparisons
cross.name: coarse_native_events

cross.help: Flag comparison as lattice-limited below this fraction of span-covered units able to reach the native threshold. Necessary reachability only, not sensitivity or a fit to observed agreement.
cross.label: Minimum lattice-capable fraction
cross.name: lattice_capable_fraction

families.help: 50 is strict; 99.9 accepts any state compatible under the native predictive test. Uses the upper predictive-tail interval bound, not a posterior probability. Never forces a rejected or unassessed match. Does not refit models.
families.label: Assignment compatibility reference (%)
families.name: assignment_reference_percent

families.help: Retain a tested alternative when recurring physical molecules distinguish it from every proposed replacement in both directions. Does not veto promotion or rerun Monte Carlo. 0 reproduces historical retirement.
families.label: Alternative retention: witnesses per direction
families.name: minimum_retention_groups

families.help: Show a fitted population state only when it is the primary explanation for at least this many independent evidence units. All fitted alternatives remain in the frozen audit evidence.
families.label: Minimum recurrent-state molecules
families.name: minimum_display_primary_units

input.help: Only for BAMs without MA/Ma: explicitly declare whether as/al and ns/nl coordinates use stored SEQ or molecular orientation. Disabled uses molecular when the header shows fibertools wrote the tags (a fibertools nucleosome command with no later FiberHMM caller), otherwise stops; it never guesses or flips REV from the data. The verified ind 2–4 h input uses seq.
input.label: Legacy Hia5 MSP/nucleosome tag frame
input.name: legacy_hia5_annotation_frame

input.help: Re-score fixed MSPs with the multi-interval decoder. Original BAM calls remain untouched in the native layer.
input.label: Replay corrected native TF decoder
input.name: correct_native

input.help: Use the production DddA mCG rate correction at tagged CpGs, in native replay and every downstream lattice score. Untagged observations are unchanged.
input.label: Honor DddA mCG substrate annotations
input.name: ddda_m5c_correction

recaller.help: 0 = all molecules; 2000 is a good cap for deep data (thousands of reads per site). Stable hash sample per dataset and chemical channel, independently in each discovery tile, after evidence filters and duplicate collapse.
recaller.label: Discovery molecules per channel (0 = all)
recaller.name: max_discovery_molecules

recaller.help: 0 = all molecules; 2000 is a good cap for deep data (thousands of reads per site). Score the same discovered catalogue on a stable sample per dataset and chemical channel in each scoring window. Prevalence uses the selected eligible molecules.
recaller.label: Quantification molecules per channel (0 = all)
recaller.name: max_quantification_molecules

recaller.help: Stable molecule hash seed shared across overlapping tiles; independent of the discovery initialization seed.
recaller.label: Molecule sampling seed
recaller.name: sample_seed

rescue.help: Separate opt-in layer. Existing TFs and nucleosomes are obstacles. Fold-excluded source geometry must support each addition.
rescue.label: Add strictly supported uncalled footprints
rescue.name: enabled

rescue.help: Bounded proposal grid for the explicitly named strict-detection auxiliary only. Not native CR variation, assay resolution, or an SR tolerance. Every addition also needs an independently trained full-grid native shape check with zero extra bp allowance.
rescue.label: Strict auxiliary proposal radius (±bp/edge)
rescue.name: proposal_edge_radius_bp

rescue.help: Opposite strand is meaningful only for strand-resolved chemistries; pooled enables within-dataset CR recall.
rescue.label: Rescue source population
rescue.name: source_mode

split.help: Retain original outer spans. Compare intact spans with internal accessible separators and CR-like protected pieces.
split.label: Test CR-supported nucleosome splits
split.name: enabled

split.help: Both ends of a proposed protected piece must match a supported CR class.
split.label: CR matching edge allowance (±bp)
split.name: ambiguity_bp

split.help: No cap on the number of compatible separators or protected pieces.
split.label: Maximum internal separator width
split.name: maximum_gap_bp

sr.help: Current harmonization changes only measurement-equivalent native edges. Historical fitted engines retain their original strand-specific rules.
sr.label: Normalize boundaries with SR
sr.name: enabled

sr.help: Each edge and their joint change must pass this native-likelihood loss budget.
sr.label: Maximum native edge-loss odds
sr.name: loss_odds

sr.help: Do not change which recipient opportunities are protected.
sr.label: Only projection-equivalent changes
sr.name: projection_only
